Oracle (NYSE:ORCL) announced plans to raise $20 billion through a combination of equity and debt offerings as the enterprise software company seeks additional funding for its expanding artificial intelligence and cloud computing infrastructure. The announcement triggered a sharp decline in its shares, reflecting investor concerns about rising capital requirements, borrowing levels and potential shareholder dilution.

The company priced an offering of 86.2 million shares at $116 each, representing an 11.2% discount to Friday's closing price. The equity sale is expected to generate approximately $10 billion, while a separate bond offering will raise another $10 billion.

Oracle shares fell 8.8% to $119.22 following the fundraising announcement on Monday, extending their decline for the year to approximately 39%.

Oracle's planned stock sale involves 86.2 million shares priced at $116 each, allowing the company to raise approximately $10 billion before accounting for offering expenses.

The pricing represents an 11.2% discount to the previous Friday's closing share price, reflecting the terms offered to investors participating in the transaction.

Bloomberg News first reported the pricing details of the equity offering.

The decision to issue additional shares comes as Oracle faces substantial funding requirements associated with its AI infrastructure investments.

While the offering provides access to new capital without increasing debt, it also expands the company's share count, potentially diluting existing shareholders.

The announcement placed pressure on Oracle's stock, which declined 8.8% to $119.22 during Monday's trading session.

The latest fall brought the company's year-to-date share price losses to approximately 39%, highlighting the market's concerns about the financial demands of its expansion strategy.

Alongside the equity offering, Oracle is raising approximately $10 billion through the sale of bonds.

The debt offering consists of five fixed-rate tranches with maturities ranging from 2029 to 2046.

Interest rates on the securities range from 7% to 8.65%, reflecting the financing costs associated with Oracle's borrowing requirements.

The final offering did not include the floating-rate tranche that had appeared in an earlier regulatory filing.

The announcement also affected Oracle's existing debt securities.

According to Tradeweb data, the company's 6.85% bonds maturing in 2066 declined by more than 1.2 cents on the dollar.

The movement reflected pressure in the bond market as investors assessed the implications of additional borrowing and Oracle's substantial capital expenditure commitments.

Oracle said the proceeds from the stock and bond offerings would be available for general corporate purposes.

Potential uses include capital expenditure, repayment of existing debt, acquisitions, dividend payments and share repurchases.

The fundraising forms part of Oracle's broader strategy to expand its cloud infrastructure and increase computing capacity for artificial intelligence workloads.

The company has committed significant resources to developing data centre infrastructure as demand for AI computing services continues to grow.

However, the scale of these investments has raised questions about the timing of financial returns and the company's ability to balance expansion with cash generation.

Oracle indicated last week that capital expenditure would reach its highest levels during the current fiscal year and the following year.

The company also committed to raising no more than $20 billion in additional AI-related financing through fiscal 2030.

Oracle's investment programme supports an ambitious expansion strategy aimed at more than tripling annual revenue by fiscal 2030.

The company expects revenue to exceed $225 billion by that year, compared with $67.36 billion reported for fiscal 2026.

Management also projects adjusted earnings of more than $21 per share in fiscal 2030.

For fiscal 2027, Wall Street analysts currently expect adjusted earnings of $8.14 per share, according to data compiled by LSEG.

Achieving the longer-term targets will depend on Oracle's ability to convert its infrastructure investments into sustained revenue growth and improved profitability.

The company is seeking to strengthen its position in the rapidly expanding AI cloud market, where it competes with larger technology companies that have substantial financial resources.

Oracle has provided investors with a timeline for when its investment programme could begin generating positive free cash flow.

Chief Financial Officer Hilary Maxson said last week that the company expects free cash flow to turn positive during the second half of fiscal 2028.

The announcement helped lift Oracle shares by approximately 11% on Wednesday, as investors responded to the prospect of improved cash generation.

However, Monday's fundraising announcement renewed attention on the amount of external capital required to support the company's expansion before reaching that milestone.

Oracle reported $125.34 billion in notes payable and other borrowings as of August 31.

The debt position is substantial relative to the company's fiscal 2026 revenue of $67.36 billion, making financing costs and cash flow generation important considerations

Oracle(NYSE:ORCL)은 기업용 소프트웨어 회사가 확장되는 인공 지능 및 클라우드 컴퓨팅 인프라를 위한 추가 자금을 모색함에 따라 지분 및 부채 제공을 통해 200억 달러를 조달할 계획을 발표했다. 이 발표는 자본 요구 사항 증가, 차입 수준 및 잠재적 주주 희석에 대한 투자자의 우려를 반영하여 주가의 급격한 하락을 촉발했다.
회사는 금요일 종가 대비 11.2% 할인된 8,620만 주 공모 가격을 주당 116달러로 책정했다. 지분 매각을 통해 약 100억 달러가 창출될 것으로 예상되며, 별도의 채권 발행을 통해 추가로 100억 달러가 조달될 것으로 예상된다.
Oracle 주가는 월요일 자금 조달 발표 이후 8.8% 하락한 119.22달러를 기록했으며, 올해 하락폭은 약 39%로 늘어났다.
Oracle의 계획된 주식 매각에는 주당 116달러의 가격으로 8,620만 주가 포함되며, 이를 통해 회사는 공모 비용을 계산하기 전에 약 100억 달러를 조달할 수 있다.
가격은 거래에 참여하는 투자자에게 제공되는 조건을 반영하여 전주 금요일 종가 대비 11.2% 할인된 가격이다.
Bloomberg News는 주식 공모의 가격 세부 사항을 처음으로 보도했다.
추가 주식을 발행하기로 한 결정은 Oracle이 AI 인프라 투자와 관련된 상당한 자금 요구 사항에 직면해 있기 때문에 나온 것이다.
이 제안은 부채를 늘리지 않고도 새로운 자본에 대한 접근을 제공하는 동시에 회사의 주식 수를 확대하여 잠재적으로 기존 주주를 희석시킵니다.
이 발표는 월요일 거래 세션 동안 8.8% 하락한 $119.22를 기록한 Oracle의 주식에 압력을 가했다.
최근 가을에 회사의 연초 현재 주가 손실은 약 39%에 이르렀으며, 이는 확장 전략의 재정적 수요에 대한 시장의 우려를 부각시켰다.
Oracle은 주식 공모와 함께 채권 매각을 통해 약 100억 달러를 조달하고 있다.
채권 발행은 2029년부터 2046년까지 만기를 갖는 5개의 고정 금리 트렌치로 구성된다.
유가증권에 대한 이자율은 7%에서 8.65% 사이이며 이는 Oracle의 차입 요건과 관련된 금융 비용을 반영한다.
최종 제안에는 이전 규제 서류에 나타난 변동 금리 트랜치가 포함되지 않았다.
